title: The Human Heart
overview: A schematic front view of the human heart. It shows the four chambers, two upper atria and two lower ventricles, the four valves between and above them, and the large blood vessels at the top. The right side of the heart is coloured blue for deoxygenated blood and the left side red for oxygenated blood. Arrows show blood flowing down through each side and up out of the ventricles.
orientation_note: This diagram is drawn as if you are facing the patient. The patient's right side, the blue deoxygenated side, appears on the left of the page.

structures.name: Right atrium
structures.location: Upper chamber on the patient's right side. On the page it is at the upper left.
structures.function: Receives deoxygenated blood returning from the body.
structures.source_quote: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the superior and inferior venae cavae.

structures.name: Right ventricle
structures.location: Lower chamber on the patient's right side, directly below the right atrium. On the page it is at the lower left.
structures.function: Pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery, towards the lungs.
structures.source_quote: The right ventricle pumps this blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary artery.

structures.name: Left atrium
structures.location: Upper chamber on the patient's left side. On the page it is at the upper right.
structures.function: Receives oxygenated blood returning from the lungs.
structures.source_quote: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.

structures.name: Left ventricle
structures.location: Lower chamber on the patient's left side, below the left atrium. It forms the pointed tip (apex) of the heart. On the page it is at the lower right.
structures.function: Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta and on to the whole body. It has the thickest muscular wall.
structures.source_quote: The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall because it pumps blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.

structures.name: Superior vena cava
structures.location: Large vein entering the top of the right atrium.
structures.function: Returns deoxygenated blood from the head, neck and arms.

structures.name: Inferior vena cava
structures.location: Large vein entering the right atrium from below. On the page it is at the far left edge.
structures.function: Returns deoxygenated blood from the lower body.

structures.name: Pulmonary artery
structures.location: Vessel rising from the top of the right ventricle, near the centre of the diagram, just to the page-left of the aorta.
structures.function: Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

structures.name: Pulmonary veins
structures.location: Vessels entering the left atrium from the side. On the page they are at the far right edge.
structures.function: Carry oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium.

structures.name: Aorta
structures.location: Large artery rising from the top of the left ventricle, near the centre of the diagram.
structures.function: Carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the whole body.

structures.name: Tricuspid valve
structures.location: Between the right atrium and the right ventricle.
structures.function: Lets blood flow from the right atrium into the right ventricle and stops it flowing back.
structures.source_quote: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle.

structures.name: Mitral valve
structures.location: Between the left atrium and the left ventricle.
structures.function: Lets blood flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle and stops it flowing back. Also called the bicuspid valve.
structures.source_quote: The mitral (bicuspid) valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle.

structures.name: Pulmonary valve
structures.location: At the exit of the right ventricle, where the pulmonary artery begins.
structures.function: Opens to let blood leave the right ventricle for the lungs and closes to stop it flowing back.

structures.name: Aortic valve
structures.location: At the exit of the left ventricle, where the aorta begins.
structures.function: Opens to let blood leave the left ventricle for the body and closes to stop it flowing back.

structures.name: Interventricular septum
structures.location: Thick muscular wall running down the middle, between the two ventricles.
structures.function: Separates the right and left ventricles so oxygenated and deoxygenated blood do not mix.
structures.source_quote: The interventricular septum is a thick muscular wall that separates the right and left ventricles.

structures.name: Chordae tendineae
structures.location: Not shown in this diagram. The lecture notes say they anchor the atrioventricular valves to the ventricle walls.
structures.function: Stop the tricuspid and mitral valve flaps turning inside out when the ventricles contract.
structures.source_quote: The atrioventricular valves are anchored to the ventricle walls by the chordae tendineae.

processes.name: Path of blood through the heart

steps.text: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium through the superior and inferior venae cavae.
The right atrium contracts and blood passes through the tricuspid valve.
The right ventricle contracts, pushing blood through the pulmonary valve.
The pulmonary artery carries the blood to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.
Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.
The left atrium contracts and blood passes through the mitral valve.
The left ventricle contracts strongly, pushing blood through the aortic valve.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood out to the whole body.

quiz.question: Which chamber pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
quiz.explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aortic valve into the aorta.

quiz.question: Which valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
quiz.explanation: The mitral, or bicuspid, valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle.

quiz.question: Where does the pulmonary artery carry blood?
quiz.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

quiz.question: On a standard anatomical diagram, which side of the page shows the patient's left ventricle?
options: The left side of the page
The right side of the page
quiz.explanation: Diagrams are drawn as if you face the patient, so the patient's left appears on the right of the page.

quiz.question: What separates the right and left ventricles?
quiz.explanation: The interventricular septum is the muscular wall between the two ventricles.
